messages:
maria_g: putting up a quick thread — I'm going to draft an RFC/mini-PRD for customer-managed egress + DNS handoff for Private deployments. want to capture requirements, acceptance criteria, and edge cases. can folks weigh in? link: https://go/repo/rfc-egress-dns (WIP)

alex_h: +1. main scope idea: two supported patterns — (A) customer-routed egress (we hand customer a static route + BGP optional) and (B) outbound-proxy/NAT managed by customer. also need explicit DNS handoff for split-horizon and optional TLS termination.

sanjay_r: couple of gotchas to call out early: overlapping CIDRs (customer might use 10.0.0.0/8), asymmetric routing (return path issues), MTU/path MTU discovery problems with encapsulation, conntrack table exhaustion on NAT gateways.

tara_ops: provider support matrix is important. AWS: TGW/VPC peering options, GCP: VPC-SC, Azure: vnet peering + forced tunneling. also whether BGP is required for GA or static routes are acceptable.

caroline_pm: customer asks we've seen: keep client source IPs for allowlists, predictable egress IPs for third-party APIs, and the ability to bring-your-own-NAT device (appliance). they'd like these as distinct product options.

deploy-bot: build 3892 succeeded for infra/routing-sim — test harness updated. :white_check_mark:

maria_g: proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
1) Docs + RFC describing both patterns and failure modes
2) End-to-end test that validates DNS handoff (split-horizon) and egress path for at least AWS and on-prem lab
3) GA support matrix: AWS/GCP/Azure + on-prem appliance w/ static route + basic BGP test
4) Ability to surface customer egress IP(s) in Console and API
5) Security review passed (no secrets leaked, KMS/HSM integration validated)

alex_h: add technical acceptance checks:
- traffic path verification: use `curl --resolve` & `dig @` tests
- NAT health: conntrack metrics and limit alerts configured
- MTU tests: run `tracepath` for encapsulated flows
- DNS TTL/propagation tests for split-horizon entries

sanjay_r: quick config example to include in RFC (very rough):
```
customer_vpc: 10.40.0.0/16
redwood_tunnel: 169.254.200.0/30
static-route: 10.40.0.0/16 via 169.254.200.1
# BGP optional
bgp: enabled
asn: 65020
```
verification: `ss -tnp | grep redwood` and `traceroute -n -T 8.8.8.8`

tara_ops: support/playbook items to prepare and include:
- onboarding checklist (CIDR check, required firewall rules, expected egress IPs)
- rollback plan (remove static route, switch to hosted egress)
- runbook for asymmetric routing: how to inspect path and force symmetric path if needed
- customer-level QoS notes (MTU, TCP MSS clamping)

caroline_pm: prioritization note: two enterprise prospects are blocked until we can guarantee stable egress IPs + split-horizon DNS. we should target a gated beta in ~6 weeks, GA in Q3. need eng estimate.

alex_h: rough resource estimate: core infra + ops + QA: ~6 weeks for beta (1 SWE + 1 infra SWE + 0.5 SRE + docs). GA adds another 4–6 weeks for expanded provider matrix, security signoff, and support docs.

maria_g: action items: alex to draft tech section + acceptance criteria, sanjay to add config examples + tests, tara to draft onboarding/runbook, caroline to consolidate customer asks and prioritize. i'll assemble RFC by EOD Friday and ping reviewers (@security-bot, @platform-leads).

security-bot: Security checklist reminder: run threat-model -> CI secrets scan -> KMS integration smoke tests.

maria_g: thanks — if anyone has strong objections to the scope, flag now. otherwise i'll start the RFC PR and tag people for review. :shipit:
